title: Redwood Security Review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC (ClearHealth)
summary: Redwood team reviewed SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning options and walked through RBAC/least-privilege roles. ClearHealth requested details on audit logs, KMS/encryption, data residency for PHI, and admin separation. Action items: send SOC 2 and ISO docs, SCIM mapping template, test tenant and guide, and schedule an ops deep-dive for SCIM attribute mapping and pilot plan.
topics: SSO / SAML flow and IDP requirements
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Aisha, Ravi / Sara, Tom, Priya, Jared

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we know your time is tight so we'll run through SSO and scim for redwood and then dive into role model and audit logs.
00:12 Sara: great thanks, quick context we're clearing security for a potential pilot. we handle PHI and the legal team wants data residency and strong least-privilege.
00:25 Liam: quick intro, i'm liam, solutions engineer. i'll show the flow and typical scim mapping patterns. there may be a few typos in my slides, sorry in advance.
00:40 Tom: one ask up front, we use okta but also have a couple customers on auth0; we'd like to know if both are supported and any gotchas.
00:52 Maya: yes okta/auth0/aws cognito supported; we do SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. most large customers use okta and we have a pre-built integration.
01:10 Liam: technical bit: we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows. metadata exchange is standard -- entityID, ACS url, cert fingerprint. for SCIM, we accept push provisioning for users and groups, with delta syncs.
01:32 Priya: for groups, can we map Okta groups to redwood roles? we want product teams to have write access and security only audit read.
01:45 Liam: yes, group-to-role mapping is configurable; common pattern: 'redwood-admin', 'redwood-power-user', 'redwood-viewer'. you can map scim group.displayName to role. we'll send the mapping template.
02:02 Sara: how do you handle account owners vs billing admins? we need separation of duties.
02:12 Ravi: we recommend separate roles: billing-admin (stripe/billing UI) and platform-admin (deploy, model rollouts). billing is gated by SSO group and we can create service accounts for automation with restricted scopes.
02:28 Tom: what's the onboarding flow? we want just-in-time provisioning if possible, rather than pre-provisioning everyone.
02:36 Liam: JIT provisioning via SAML is supported for sign-in, but for SCIM we can provision users ahead of time. many customers do both: SCIM to seed users and groups, and JIT as fallback. note: SCIM push supports incremental update events, but if your idp limits rate we'll throttle.
03:05 Maya: quick note on SCIM attributes we commonly sync: externalId, userName/email, displayName, title, manager, groups. if you have custom attributes, we can map via claims.
03:20 Jared: any constraints on usernames? we prefer emails as primary.
03:26 Liam: primary identifier is userName (email). we strongly recommend email as stable id.
03:40 Sara: audit logs: retention, format, and access controls are important. can you export logs to our SIEM?
03:50 Ravi: yes, we stream audit logs to customer S3 or to a push endpoint; we also have an S3 connector for Splunk/QRadar ingestion. retention is configurable; default 90 days in hosted tier but enterprise can extend.
04:12 Sara: for HIPAA we need at least 7 years for some artifacts. can you support long-term retention?
04:20 Ravi: yes, for enterprise we can archive logs to a customer managed S3 with lifecycle policy for long-term retention. this can be part of a dedicated contract.
04:35 Priya: are logs tamper-evident?
04:40 Ravi: logs are immutable once written, and we keep checksums. customer-managed S3 plus object lock is an option for WORM-like retention.
04:55 Tom: encryption questions: at rest and in transit, and KMS integration.
05:04 Ravi: everything in transit uses TLS 1.2+, and at-rest encryption uses AES-256. for keys we support a Redwood-managed KMS or customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM for dedicated/private. we can rotate keys on customer schedule; key usage is logged in audit trail.
05:28 Sara: will keys for PHI be stored in our account? we need sole control.
05:35 Ravi: with a private deployment or dedicated we can use customer-owned KMS keys; for hosted we offer CMKs via your AWS account for some regions. we'll follow up with exact deployment variants.
05:48 Maya: on RBAC least-privilege: typical roles we recommend and default perms: Admin = full, DevOps = deploy/manage models, Analyst = run queries/embeddings read, Viewer = read-only. you can also create custom roles and scope by project/team.
06:10 Priya: we need role scoping by project and environment (prod vs staging). is that supported?
06:18 Liam: yes, role binding supports resource scoping. you can scope roles to projects and to model routes. we also support policy-based access for canary rollouts.
06:35 Tom: how are API keys and service accounts handled? rotation policy?
06:42 Ravi: service accounts are tied to org-level or project-level with explicit scopes (generate-only, read-embeddings, write inference). keys can be short lived — we support rotating tokens and recommend <90 day rotation. you can also use OIDC tokens for ephemeral auth.
07:05 Sara: does Redwood provide an audit UI for admin actions?
07:10 Aisha: yes the Console shows admin events, token usage, per-route latencies and cost. audit can be filtered by actor and exported.
07:25 Priya: for SCIM mapping, who typically owns attribute mapping? our IdP team or Redwood?
07:32 Liam: usually jointly. we provide a default mapping and a template, your IdP team imports as an application and then we adjust any custom attributes. we'll schedule a mapping session.
07:50 Tom: are there known edge cases with Okta group nested groups or SCIM complex groups?
07:58 Liam: nested groups are handled but some idps flatten them differently; we'll test with your tenant. large groups might cause initial provisioning spikes.
08:20 Sara: data residency: our PHI must stay in US-east and EU-West per contracts. can you pin data to regions?
08:30 Ravi: yes. hosted clusters can be regionally pinned; for strict residency we recommend dedicated or private setups where we deploy your control plane and data in the chosen region. we also support cross-region replication but can disable it.
08:50 Maya: note that some Redwood features (e.g., global model catalog) may still have metadata references; we'll provide a residency diagram.
09:05 Priya: SOC 2 and ISO: do you have reports and penetration test summaries?
09:12 Maya: yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; we will share the attestation and a redacted pentest summary under an NDA.
09:24 Sara: ok great. can you also share your subprocessor list and data flow diagrams?
09:30 Maya: yes, we'll include that in the package.
09:38 Tom: legal will want encryption in transit proof and key handling steps.
09:44 Ravi: we'll include KMS architecture and customer key lifecycle.
09:50 Priya: can we see a demo of SCIM provisioning in our tenant?
09:55 Liam: yes we can provision a test tenant and run a live sync. we'll need an okta admin invite and a test idp config.
10:10 Maya: onto role separation: for least-privilege we propose creating these groups: security-audit (read-only audit logs), infra-admin (deploy and manage), billing-admin (billing UI only), product-publish (can manage model routes), service-accounts (automation only).
10:30 Sara: sounds good. what's the default for new users?
10:34 Liam: by default new users are viewer until assigned groups. optionally you can use SCIM to assign initial groups.
10:45 Jared: what about emergency access / break glass?
10:49 Ravi: we support time-bound elevated access and require justification with an audit event. break-glass tokens are single-use and logged.
11:05 Priya: what's the recommended test plan for pilot? sync 50 users, 3 groups, test provisioning, check audit logs, run basic inference and encryption check.
11:14 Maya: yep that's what we normally do for pilots. estimate 2-3 weeks to run initial POC.
11:22 Sara: any contractual SLAs for audit log delivery and availability?
11:27 Maya: in enterprise contracts yes; hosted standard we publish uptime SLOs and dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime and latency guarantees.
11:36 Tom: about SCIM rate limits, any specifics we should be aware of?
11:41 Liam: SCIM has per-tenant rate limits to protect the API; we'll share the numbers but typical customers are fine. for initial bulk provisioning we'll coordinate a window.
11:55 Maya: ok we'll recap next steps now.
12:00 Maya: action items: maya send SOC2/ISO and processor list; liam send SCIM mapping template and test tenant invite; ravi draft KMS and key lifecycle doc; aisha coordinate pilot timeline; sara will provide okta admin contact.
12:20 Sara: thanks all, feel confident so far. we'll review and get legal involved.
12:30 Maya: great we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the SCIM mapping session. thanks everyone.
12:40 End of meeting
